title: Policy & Procedure (P&P) for the sorting, storage, handling, transportation, and disposal of hazardous materials
html:
• Purpose: To protect the health and well being of all employees, patients, and visitors and to avoid exposing unauthorized individuals to a hazardous environment.
  • Scope : Hospital Wide

3. DEFINITION

Hazardous materials are a material which, because of their chemical, physical or Biological properties, poses a potential risk to life, health, the environment, or Property when not properly contained.

It includes materials that are explosive, flammable, combustible, corrosive, reactive, poisonous, biological or radioactive. They can be solid, liquid or Gaseous

  • Policy

Current environmental regulations make an in-house industrial hazardous materials team a necessary part of many industrial operations. However, the need for prompt response to hazardous materials releases and proper mitigation of these incidents often makes having an own team a necessity.

Starting a team and managing the operations of the team are critical tasks. During a start up we must organize resources, plan for handling emergencies, evaluate and purchase equipment, and train response personnel. These tasks must also be part of a continuing management program to keep the team ready for emergencies.

4.1 CLASSIFICATION OF HAZARDOUS MATERIALS

Class 1: Explosives-Materials in this category include projectiles as well as sensitive and insensitive explosives. All must be handled with extreme caution. They should never be shaken or dropped and should be kept away from open flames.

Class 2: Hazardous Gases-This class includes flammable and nonflammable compressed gasses as well as poisonous gases. Class 3: Flammable Liquids-This class includes both flammable liquids with a

Flashpoint below 140 degrees F and combustible liquids with a flash point between 141 and 200 degrees F.

Class 4: Flammable Solids-This includes spontaneously combustible and "dangerous when wet" solids that become combustible when brought into contact with water.

Class 5: Oxidizers-This class includes organic peroxide. These substances can become catalysts for fire hazards.

Class 6: Toxic Materials-This includes inhalation hazards, other poisons, and infectious substances. Swallowing, bodily contact, or inhalation of gases released by toxic substances may cause irritation of skin and mucous membranes, or in more severe cases, serious illness. Contact a physician immediately if exposed.

Class 7: Radioactive Materials (Not Applicable)

Class 8: Corrosive Materials-Corrosive materials can harm living tissue and nonliving matter, such as steel, on contact.

Class 9: Biohazard agents: includes biological waste, mercury.

Class 10: Hazardous Chemical hazardous chemicals as any chemical that is a

Physical or health hazard and which meets the definition of:

(a) Carcinogen,

(b) Corrosive,

(c) Highly-toxic,

(d) Irritant, and/or Toxic.

4.2 LABELING OF HAZARDOUS MATERIALS

Any hazardous materials received in the wards / units should have proper signages on it.

4.3 Storage of the HAZMAT material

  • All hazardous material are segregated and stored separately. Store in designated, secure areas
  • Ensure:
    • Proper ventilation
    • Spill containment systems
    • Fire safety measures

Specific Requirements

  • Chemicals: Store per compatibility (flammable, corrosive, etc.)
  • Biomedical waste: Store < 48 hours (or per local regulation)
  • Sharps: Use puncture-proof containers

4.4 Inventory of Hazmat: All the hazardous material has a defined inventory and maximum storage quantity unit wise and store level.

4.5 Hazardous Materials Handling

  • There shall be identified list of hazardous materials in the hospital.
  • The staff shall be educated about the handling and storage of those materials.
  • The hazardous materials shall be stored in the designated areas marked for the same.
  • The storage of hazardous material shall be done according to the consumption pattern in that particular area.
  • There shall be a HAZMAT team to take care of hazardous materials spillage in the hospital.

4.6 Spill kit

Spill kit is available in each unit for MINOR spills and with Hazmat team for Major spills.

4.7 HAZMAT TEAM COMPOSITION

Hazmat team constitutes of the Supervisors on duty from the following Departments who will be available round the clock for Management of Hazardous Material Spills:

  • Security
  • Housekeeping
  • Engineering
  • Nursing

4.9 TRAINING

Training classes are conducted for the HAZMAT team members who will in turn educate the staff under their supervision.

4.10 RESPONSIBILITIES

4.10.1 Responsibilities of Hazmat Team members:

  • Available round the clock.
  • Reach site of emergency as soon as possible.
  • Come equipped with suitable/necessary equipment/material.
  • Security:
    • Cordon off the area using suitable tools.
    • Manage personnel in surrounding area.
  • Engineering:
    • Provide support to any electrical or mechanical requirements/management.
  • Nursing:
    • Attend to/monitor emergency medical situation.
  • Housekeeping:
    • Containing/managing the spill.
  • Ensure that sufficient quantities and appropriate types of spill control materials are available to contain and clean up a minor spill.
  • Ensure that any required personal protective equipment (e.g. eyewear or gloves) is available.
  • Ensure that spill control materials are located in a readily accessible location.
  • Record information regarding any spills using the Spill Report Form. Completed forms must be submitted to HAZMAT TEAM INCHARGE (Housekeeping In charge)

4.10.2 Responsibilities of Staff:

  • Be familiar with the properties and hazards of the materials at work site.
  • Before beginning work with a chemical, be aware of its hazards and the use of appropriate personal protective equipment.
  • Ensure proper reporting procedures are followed in the event of a spill.

5. MANAGEMENT OF HAZARDOUS MATERIAL SPILLS

The notification, building evacuation, and spill reporting procedures outlined below apply to chemical, biological, and radioactive spills.

5.1 MINOR SPILLS

5.4.1Blood spills:

  • If less than 20 –30 ml.
  • Wear PPE (Gloves, Mask, Gown)
  • Pick up any broken glass with tongs or other mechanical device. Do not use your hands.
  • Place absorbent materials (cotton) over the spill, making sure not to spread liquid.
  • Put 1%sodium hypochlorite and keep it for 20 minutes.
  • Dispose off all contaminated material in a yellow plastic bag, label it and contact housekeeping for disposal.
  • Complete a Spills Report Form and submit to Quality Dept.
  • The person responsible for spill may fill up the form and counter signed by the in-charge of that area. However, the over all responsibility will be of in-charge.

5.2 Formalin spillage:

  • Less than 20 –30 ml of formaldehyde spills.
  • Wear rubber gloves or double vinyl gloves and protective eyewear.
  • Clean up the spill with an absorbent material.
  • Wash the area with copious amounts of water.
  • Place all contaminated disposable material in a double yellow bag and label as
    • Hazardous waste,
    • Name of the Substance: Formaldehyde
    • Date & Time of spill
    • Quantity of spill:
    • Department / Unit:
    • Signature:
    • Contact housekeeping to promptly remove hazardous waste.
  • Do not dispose off in general waste.
  • Complete a Spills Report Form and submit to Quality Dept.
  • The person responsible for spill may fill up the form and counter signed by the in-charge of that area. However, the over all responsibility will be of in-charge.

5.3 ETO SPILL

Primary Emergency Procedures:

  • Evacuate the immediate area and if possible, remove any injured persons.
  • Raise an alarm. Notify the Hazmat team. Seal the area as best as possible.
  • Contact the necessary companies who installed / manufactured the unit.
  • Persons in contact with ETO should immediately remove contaminated clothing and wash or shower to remove any ETO from skin. Bring to Emergency Room for proper care.
  • Complete a Spills Report Form and submit to Quality dept.
  • The person responsible for spill may fill up the form and counter signed by the in-charge of that area. However, the over all responsibility will be of in-charge.

5.4 Hazardous material spills (other than mercury, formalin & ETO)

  • Rescue anyone immediately affected by the emergency. Only perform rescue if it does not put you to great risk.
  • If emergency involves a fire, use the manual pull box to activate the fire alarm.
  • For spills that do not involve fire or explosion, contact hazardous material team and describe the emergency. Request Hazmat team for chemical or radiological incidents.
  • Warn others in the area about emergency and stay clear of the spill area

5.5 Clean up of Small Chemical Spills

If less than 20 –30 ml.

Review Material Safety Data Sheets (MSDS) or other references for recommended spill cleanup methods and materials, and the need for personalprotective equipment (e.g., respirator, gloves)

Pick up any broken glass with tongs or other mechanical device. Do not use your hands.

Place absorbent materials (Cottons) over the spill, making sure not to spread liquid.

Dispose off all contaminated material in a plastic bag, label it and contact housekeeping for disposal.

Wash the area with copious amounts of water.

Complete a Spills Report Form and submit to the Quality Dept.

the person responsible for spill may fill up the form and counter signed by the in-charge of that area. However, the over all responsibility will be of in-charge.

5.6 MAJOR SPILLS (If more than 20 –30 ml).

5.6.1 Blood Spill:

Call hazmat Team by dialing “7502/ tell HAZMAT code in Walky Talky & restrict the area.

Hazmat team:

Wear PPE (Gloves, Mask, Gown)

Pick up any broken glass with tongs or other mechanical device.

Place absorbent materials (cotton) over the spill,

Put 10%sodium hypochlorite and kept it for20- 30 minutes.

Dispose off all contaminated material in a yellow plastic bag, label it

Complete a Spills Report Form and submit to the Quality Dept.

5.6.2 Mercury spills (Thermometer/B.p. Apparatus breakage)

(All mercury spills are major spills)

  • Isolate the area of spill by placing a box or waste can over the spill to reduce the spread of mercury vapors.
  • Notify everyone to remain clear of the area.
  • Immediately contact Hazmat Team through “7502/ tell HAZMAT code in Walky Talky”
  • Hazmat team will arrive at the spot and cleanup the spill
  • After collecting mercury with the help of two stiff papers send it to biomedical dept for further management.
  • Fill the spill form and send it to Quality Dept.

5.6.3. Formalin spills

  • If more than 20 –30 ml of formaldehyde spills, employees are not to clean it up.
  • Immediately evacuate the area & close all the doors.
  • Alert others not to enter the area.
  • Contact Hazardous Materials Response Team.
  • Do not re-enter the area until it has been declared clear by the HAZMAT team.

5.9 Ethylene Oxide Emergency

  • After carrying out the procedures mentioned in Primary Emergency Procedure.
  • Engineering and security is responsible for bringing the emergency under control. This includes rescue, fire fighting, and contamination control through clean up or other methods.

5.7 Hazardous material spill (other than mercury, formalin, & ETO)

Clean up of large spills

  • Large chemical spills are greater than 20 – 30 cc.
  • Immediately evacuate the area and close all doors. Notify others not to enter the area.
  • Activate fire alarm by pulling the nearest manual pull box.
  • Contact Hazmat team by Dialing “7502/ tell HAZMAT code in Walky Talky
  • Inform the location, name of material, and approximate quantity.
  • Do not re-enter the area until advised by Hazmat team.

5.8 Employee contamination during Chemical spills

  • If the skin becomes contaminated with hazardous material, wash the affected are thoroughly with copious amounts of water. If available, use an emergency shower for at least 15 minutes.
  • If hazardous material is splashed in the eyes, flush the eyes immediately with water, preferably using an eye wash station, for at least 15 minutes.
  • Remove grossly contaminated clothing immediately. Place the contaminated clothing in a plastic bag.
  • Report the spill to the supervisor of the area and seek medical attention. If possible, bring the label or information on the chemical with you.

6. PROCEDURE

HAZMAT TEAM

  • HAZMAT team to be available round the clock for cleaning up large spills of hazardous materials.
  • In case of an incident / accident to be contacted is the Exchange through the telephone number “7502/ tell HAZMAT code in Walky Talky” to intimate members of Hazmat team.
  • Hazmat team to reach the site with appropriate Personal Protective Equipment and Absorbents and Containers to control the situation.
  • Contaminated waste to be placed in a Yellow bag with proper labeling i.e.
    • Name of the Substance:
    • Date & Time of Incident:
    • Unit / Area:
    • Quantity of Spill:
    • Signature:

and to be sent to Waste Disposal area

  • Other Hazardous material will be handed over to an outside agency for disposal.
  • HAZMAT Spill report form to be filled up and sent to the Quality Department.

Annexure

– Spill Report Form

Biological Hazards:

All biomedical waste is considered hazardous and treated with all universal precaution

Waste Disposal: Waste disposal is done according to the color code and as per norms within the unit.

Trash or infected waste:

All mentioned waste is collected in appropriate colored double bags and clearly labeled with infected sticker and sealed and sent for incineration.

Linen:

All the linen is double maroon colored bag and infected linen shall be placed the double maroon colored bag and tied. It is sealed with an infected linen sticker and sent directly to the laundry without counting the contents. Disposable drapes are discarded in yellow dust bin and sent.

Unused blood: All unused blood bag are discarded after autoclave.

Training for Housekeeping: All the housekeeping is trained at regular interval in universal precaution and waste management and linen protocol.

Transportation

Internal Transport

  • Use closed, leak-proof trolleys
  • Follow designated routes
  • Avoid patient/public areas when possible

External Transport

  • Use authorized, licensed transporters
  • Ensure:
    • Proper documentation (manifests)
    • Labeling per regulations
    • Emergency response information available

FINAL DISPOSAL: Final disposal of all hazardous materials which are collected in separate cans is outsourced services.
